the reaction volumes of M(n+/(Mn-1)+) couples are estimated from the M(n+/(Nn- 1+)) couples by the theoretical equations proposed on the basis of MSA, and the electron self-exchanges of [Ni(tcn)(2)](4+/3+) and [Co(en)(3)](4+/2+) couples obey the Marcusian behavior, while that of [Ni(tn)(2)] (3+/2+) couples does not obey

the reaction volumes for the M(n+/(Mn- 1) +) redox couples can be estimated from the reaction volumes for their self-exchange reactions and the reaction volume of the M(n+ + 2) + 2e(-) --> M(n+)/(Mn- 2) redox couple, and that the electron self- exchange reaction of the [Ni (tacn)(2) ](3+/2) + couple obeys the conventional Marcus theory
the activation volume for the self-exchange reaction in aqueous solution was estimated for the first time, and that it is consistent with the theoretical estimation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the oxidation reaction of [Ni(iii)(tacn)(2)(aq)(+) by [Fe(ii)(o-phen)(3)(aq)(2+)] in aqueous acidic medium at elevated pressure.
the development and application of theoretical equations for the estimation of the reaction and activation volumes for electron transfer processes.

the oxidation reaction of [Ni(ligand)](2+) (ligand = 1,4, 7-triazacycloonane) by [Fe(o -phenanthroline)](3+) (o-phen = o-phenanthro-line) at elevated pressures and the estimation of the activation volume for the electron self-ex-change process of this redox pair.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electron self exchange of the [Ni(1)](3+/+) couple obeys the classical Marcusian behavior in the aqueous acidic solution.
the electron self- exchange reaction of the [Ni(1)](3+/+), [Ni(1)(2)](4+/3+) and [Ni(1) (3)](5+/4+) couples in aqueous acidic solutions is governed by the Marcusian theory.
the electron self exchange reaction of the [Ni(iii)/(ii)](2+) couple in aqueous acidic solutions obeys Marcusian behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the reaction volumes of M(n+/(m- 1)+)(aq) couples in solution can be theoretically predicted with the accuracy of +/-1 cm(3)mol(-1) and that the activation volumes of M(n+/m- 1+)(aq) couples can be theoretically predicted within +/-2 cm(3)mol(-1) for the electron self-exchanges of these redox couples in solution.

the electron self exchange of the [Ni(1)(2)(2+)]/[Ni(1)(3)(3+) couple is a Marcusian process in aqueous acidic solutions, and the reaction volume of the [Ni(I)](2+/+) couple is -6.8 +/- 0.5 cm(2) mol(-1) at 25 degrees C.
the reaction volume of M(n+/(m+)) couple can be estimated theoretically within the allowed uncertainty of +/-1 cm(3). mol(-1).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activation and reaction volume of the [Ni(1)](3+/+)(2+) couple in aqueous acidic solutions can be estimated from the cross reaction between [Ni(1)(2+)] and [Fe(o-ph)(3)](2+) in aqueous solutions.
the reaction volume of an electron-transfer reaction can be estimated theoretically with an accuracy of +/- 1 cm(3)/mol.
the reaction volume for a self-exchange process is a useful parameter to estimate the reaction mechanism and activation volume for a redox reaction in solution.
